# QS-PROC-01 Forging temperature control (P1)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1, line P1-L1  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L1-IH03

Scope
This quality specification establishes requirements for temperature control and coil condition monitoring for the induction billet heater identified as EQ-P1-L1-IH03 on line P1-L1 in Plant P1. The document addresses acceptance criteria, inspection frequency, inspection methods, records, and nonconformance handling for the coil and its observed effects on forging temperature control. Follow related maintenance and operational procedures cited in related documents for detailed tasks and safe work practices: MM-P1-L1-IH03, SOP-P1-L1-01, SOP-P1-L1-04.

Background and rationale
Consistent heater coil condition is a primary contributor to stable heating profiles and repeatable forging temperatures. Coil degradation, partial shorting, turn separation, or insulation breakdown will manifest as drift in heating uniformity, increased electrical losses, and potential safety hazards. Regular coil inspections reduce unplanned downtime and prevent unacceptable forging temperature variation that can produce out-of-spec parts. The coil inspection interval is selected to balance operational availability and early detection of degradation, based on historical degradation patterns and supplier guidance documented in MM-P1-L1-IH03.

Requirements table
| Item | Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coil inspection interval | The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. | Inspection completed at or before interval; documented completion entry in equipment log; no unresolved findings older than the next scheduled inspection. | MM-P1-L1-IH03 |
| Coil visual integrity | Coil surfaces free of visible insulation cracks, charring, or exposed conductors that could affect field uniformity. | No exposed conductors; no insulation delamination requiring immediate shutdown per SOP-P1-L1-01. | SOP-P1-L1-01 |
| Electrical connections | Terminal lugs and leads secured, no discoloration indicative of overheating. | Connections torque and condition per MM-P1-L1-IH03; no loose or oxidized terminals. | MM-P1-L1-IH03 |
| Cooling path | Cooling channels and flow connections free of blockage and corrosion that could alter coil operating temperature. | Visual confirmation of flow integrity; no deposits obstructing flow. | MM-P1-L1-IH03 |
| Heater-to-process performance | Forging inlet temperature stability within process capability as monitored in SOP-P1-L1-04. | Process monitoring shows stable inlet temperature profile after inspection; deviations logged and addressed. | SOP-P1-L1-04 |

Inspection method
- Preparation and safety
  - Review applicable steps in SOP-P1-L1-01 and MM-P1-L1-IH03 before beginning the inspection. Lockout and tagout per SOP-P1-L1-01 and ensure electrical isolation of EQ-P1-L1-IH03.
  - Allow the coil and surrounding structure to reach a safe condition as defined in SOP-P1-L1-01 before performing hands-on inspection.

- Visual inspection
  - Perform a systematic visual sweep of the coil exterior visible from the access point. Inspect for cracks, discoloration, deformation, insulation separation, and any foreign material adhering to coil surfaces.
  - Inspect mechanical supports and clamp points for wear or movement that could cause coil displacement.

- Electrical interface check
  - With the equipment isolated, examine terminal connections and cable entry points for signs of arcing, discoloration, or mechanical loosening. Follow connection checks in MM-P1-L1-IH03.

- Cooling inspection
  - Inspect cooling lines and fittings for signs of leakage, corrosion, or blocked passages where accessible. Confirm seals and hose conditions per MM-P1-L1-IH03.

- Functional verification
  - After reassembly and removal of lockout/tagout, perform controlled start-up per SOP-P1-L1-04. Monitor process temperature behavior and compare to expected heating profile. Document any transient anomalies.

- Use of non-destructive aids
  - Where available, employ infrared imaging or borescope inspection to reveal subsurface hot spots or internal coil defects not visible externally. Record findings in the inspection report.

Examples and interpretation
- Example: If visual inspection finds localized insulation charring without exposed conductor, clean area and schedule follow-up per MM-P1-L1-IH03. Record cleaning action and monitor at the next scheduled coil inspection.
- Example: If terminal discoloration and looseness are found, do not return the heater to service until connections are repaired and verified per MM-P1-L1-IH03. Document repair and attach post-repair verification evidence.
- Example: If cooling passage restriction is detected, isolate the cooling loop and remediate blockage. Confirm restored flow and monitor heater temperature response during the next start-up sequence.

Records to keep
- Maintain an equipment inspection log entry for EQ-P1-L1-IH03 that includes inspector name, date of inspection, scope of inspection, and a statement confirming the coil inspection interval condition: The coil inspection interval for Hot Forge induction billet heater #3 (EQ-P1-L1-IH03) is 290 hours. Attach supporting images, infrared scans, and repair orders as applicable.
- File all corrective maintenance records per MM-P1-L1-IH03 and link start-up verification records to the entry as referenced in SOP-P1-L1-04.
- Retain inspection reports and related records in the document control system in accordance with plant retention practices referenced in MM-P1-L1-IH03.

Nonconformance handling
- Immediate actions
  - If any condition is found that presents an immediate safety risk or clear electrical hazard, stop operation and place EQ-P1-L1-IH03 into an out-of-service state following SOP-P1-L1-01.
  - Initiate a nonconformance record and notify maintenance and quality leads.

- Evaluation and disposition
  - Classify findings according to severity per MM-P1-L1-IH03. For defects that may impact forging temperature control, perform containment actions such as process hold or quarantining affected lots until heater condition is verified.
  - Repair or replace defective components following MM-P1-L1-IH03 procedures. Perform re-inspection and start-up verification per SOP-P1-L1-04.

- Verification and closure
  - Document corrective actions and verification results in the EQ-P1-L1-IH03 equipment log. Nonconformance records must include reference to related repair orders and verification steps. Close nonconformances only after successful verification that heater performance and coil condition meet the acceptance criteria listed in this document.

Related documents
- MM-P1-L1-IH03
- SOP-P1-L1-01
- SOP-P1-L1-04
